who: Historian of nineteenth-century Britain and crime, University of Kentucky.

evidence.says: Kentucky lists Tammy Whitlock as an associate professor of history and names her book Crime, Gender and Consumer Culture in Nineteenth-Century England (2005).
The Tammy C. Whitlock authority cites the same 2005 book.
Anna Rachel Herrington’s 2019 Kentucky history MA thesis on commons enclosure lists Dr. Tammy Whitlock among its faculty.

notes: Matching university, field and authored book identify the LC candidate. The Herrington source is her earlier MA thesis, not the 2023 dissertation.

who: George Milton Addy, historian of modern Spain at Brigham Young University, Duke history PhD 1957.

evidence.says: BYU identifies George Milton Addy, records his Duke history PhD in 1957 and subsequent BYU faculty career through retirement in 1992.
The authority identifies George M. (George Milton) Addy and cites The Enlightenment in the University of Salamanca (1966).

notes: Full name, doctoral institution and year, field and BYU career agree with the supervisor record.

who: Patrick G. Williams, historian of Arkansas and American politics, University of Arkansas, Columbia PhD 1996.

evidence.says: A 2014 university article identifies Patrick G. Williams as an Arkansas history professor with a Columbia PhD, teaching Arkansas and American political history.
The authority for Patrick G. Williams explicitly records a Columbia University PhD in 1996.
The 2017 history newsletter says Rodney Harris’s Arkansas’s Divided Democracy: The Making of the Constitution of 1874 was directed by Patrick Williams.

notes: Exact doctoral institution and year plus the named student establish the match to Patrick G. Williams.

who: Frederick Charles Wilson, historian of medieval Anglo-French relations, McGill history PhD 1973.

evidence.says: McGill lists Frederick Charles Wilson’s Anglo-French Relations in the Reign of King Henry IV of England, 1399-1413 as a 1973 PhD thesis.

The authority expands Frederick C. Wilson to Frederick Charles Wilson and cites his McGill thesis Some aspects of the foreign policy of Richard II of England during his personal rule 1389-1399 (1960).

notes: Full name, McGill training and closely related medieval-English research identify the candidate; the 1973 doctorate matches own_phd. Ottawa employment was not independently verified.

who: Benjamin E. Wise, historian of modern America, southern history, gender and sexuality, University of Florida.

evidence.says: Florida identifies Ben Wise as an associate professor of modern American history and author of William Alexander Percy (2012).
The Benjamin E. Wise authority cites William Alexander Percy (2012).
Mallory Szymanski’s 2017 Florida dissertation on neurasthenia and men’s health names Benjamin Wise as chair.

notes: The shared book and the student’s dissertation establish the LC identity and supervisory connection.

who: Timothy S. Wolters, naval and technology historian at Iowa State University, MIT PhD.

evidence.says: Iowa State identifies Timothy S. Wolters as a history associate professor, an MIT PhD in history of science and technology, and author of Information at Sea (2013).
The Timothy S. Wolters authority cites Information at sea (2013).
The 2014-15 Iowa State catalogue lists Timothy S. Wolters as assistant professor of history with an MIT PhD dated 2004.

notes: Name, university, doctoral institution and book agree. Iowa State dates the PhD to 2004, whereas own_phd gives 2003; retain this discrepancy.

who: Anthony Edward Woods, Jr. (Tony Woods), historian of colonial Malawi, Michigan State history PhD 1991.

evidence.says: The Anthony Edward Woods authority cites Accumulation and order (1991), whose title page names Anthony Edward Woods, Jr.
Michigan State’s African history dissertation list records Tony Woods, Accumulation and order: state and society in Colonial Malawi, 1891-1929 (1991).

notes: The same dissertation title and year connect the LC identity to Michigan State’s graduate, matching own_phd. St John’s employment was not independently verified.

who: Edward Newport Wright-Rios, historian of modern Mexico at Vanderbilt, UC San Diego PhD 2004.

evidence.says: Vanderbilt identifies Edward Wright-Rios as a modern Mexican historian with a UC San Diego PhD in 2004.
The authority expands Edward N. Wright-Rios to Edward Newport Wright-Rios; it cites his 1998 work and confirmation from Vanderbilt’s registrar.
His July 2017 university CV lists a Vanderbilt MA in 1998, UC San Diego PhD in 2004, and Vanderbilt history appointments from 2004 onward.
Vanderbilt’s Lance Ingwersen biography names Edward Wright-Rios as advisor and gives the dissertation title Mexico City in the Age of Theater, 1830-1901.

notes: Vanderbilt registrar evidence, matching degrees, faculty dates and the named student establish the identity.
